sentences.text: So, um, at Fernhill I was on the lifecycle team, and we owned all the onboarding emails.
And basically activation was kind of flat, like for a long time, and leadership was worried about it.
We had a welcome series, it was five emails, and the thinking was the content wasn't strong enough.
So we looked at the data and, you know, people were actually clicking, they just weren't linking their bank.
So we changed the trigger so it fires when they stall on that step, and the design team simplified the screen.
And activation went up to about 44 percent, which was a big deal for us.
And then after that we also started looking at the second week, and we did some stuff with push notifications, and I think that helped too, but we never really measured that one properly.
